article.title: Arrested Over a Satirical Meme: A Texas Sheriff Loses Qualified Immunity
article.intro: Kolton Krottinger was arrested on a felony charge over a photoshopped Facebook joke, held on a bond that barred him from social media, and cleared when a justice of the peace found no probable cause. A federal judge has now let his civil rights suit against Hood County proceed.
article.body:
Kolton Krottinger, a Navy veteran in Hood County, Texas, was arrested on a felony charge over a satirical political meme posted to a Facebook page. The charge was thrown out for want of probable cause, and prosecutors then refused it outright. On July 20, 2026, a federal judge stripped the sheriff and the deputy who built the case of qualified immunity, and Krottinger's civil rights suit is going forward.

A photoshopped endorsement

In early October 2025, an image appeared on the Hood County Sheepdogs Facebook page — a local page that describes itself as carrying satire and jokes. The image had been altered to make it look as though Tina Brown, a regular speaker at Hood County commissioners' meetings, had endorsed Monica Brown in a Granbury ISD school board race. The two women are not allies, which was the joke.

Tina Brown reported the post to the Hood County Sheriff's Office on September 30, and deputies took her complaint on October 6.

A felony for a meme

On November 5, 2025, Krottinger was arrested on a third-degree felony charge of online impersonation. The criminal complaint was signed by investigator James Luckie; the arrest warrant was signed by a justice of the peace. Deputies seized Krottinger's phone at the arrest without a warrant. According to his lawyers, it has never been returned.

He was booked into the Hood County jail and released on a $10,000 bond carrying a condition that barred him from using social media — a speech restriction imposed on a man charged over speech. A judge later restored those rights.

Krottinger runs several Hood County news pages on Facebook and a nonprofit, Anxiety Solutions of America, which operates a ranch for veterans and first responders.

The case falls apart

It did not survive first contact with a courtroom. On December 5, 2025, Justice of the Peace Earl "Dub" Gillum discharged the charge after the state failed to establish probable cause.

On December 22, 2025, the Ellis County District Attorney's office — brought in from outside Hood County — formally refused the case, citing insufficient evidence that Krottinger had created or posted the material at all.

The suit, and the immunity ruling

On January 10, 2026, Krottinger sued in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas, represented by attorneys Brandon Grable and C.J. Grisham. The suit names Hood County along with Sheriff Roger Deeds, former deputy James Luckie, and District Attorney Ryan Sinclair in their personal capacities. It pleads violations of the First, Fourth, and Fourteenth Amendments, and of the federal Privacy Protection Act over the warrantless seizure of his phone.

Qualified immunity is the doctrine that ends most such suits before discovery. On July 20, 2026, Chief U.S. District Judge Reed O'Connor declined to apply it to Deeds and Luckie, holding that Krottinger had sufficiently alleged First Amendment retaliation, unlawful arrest, malicious prosecution, and Fourth Amendment violations. The case proceeds against them.

What remains disputed

Two things in this record do not line up, and are worth stating plainly rather than smoothing over.

  • Who made the post. In November 2025, Krottinger's own defense attorney described the meme as his, made "to poke fun at the two people who can't stand each other." The civil suit says a different administrator of the page posted it. The prosecutors who refused the case said there was insufficient evidence he created or posted the material. All three statements are on the record; they are not consistent.
  • The date of the ruling. Reporting gives both July 19 and July 20, 2026 for Judge O'Connor's order. July 20 is used above as the date given by more than one account.

What is not in dispute is the shape of it: a county arrested a man on a felony charge over a political joke, jailed him, took his phone, forbade him to speak online as a condition of release, and then could not persuade a justice of the peace that there was probable cause. The archive holds his record at Kolton Krottinger.

source_note.image: Fulton County Sheriff's Office booking photographs of the six people arrested in Atlanta on January 21, 2023, released by the Atlanta Police Department and published as a single six-up composite. The two frames here are that composite cut into cells.
source_note.watermark: The Fulton County Sheriff's seal sits in the corner of the Murphy frame and is kept. It is the issuing agency's own mark on its own record, which is the same reason the framing audit left the white margins on the 1961 Freedom Rider prints alone. What was removed from other photographs in this archive was a television station's watermark on someone else's picture.
source_note.verification: The cell-to-person assignment was not taken from the caption. Each candidate cell was put beside the image already on the record and matched by eye before anything was written.

not_changed.why: The framing audit listed him as needing a replacement source because the top of his head is clipped. There is no better source: the 640x360 frame in this archive is the same frame every outlet ran, re-encoded. The clipping is slight and the face is complete and legible, so the record keeps it. The audit entry was right that it is imperfect and wrong that it was fixable.

The other three of the six arrested that night were cropped in batch 172 from broadcast frames 524 pixels tall, which is more resolution than the official composite's 400x337 cells. Replacing them with the official photograph would look like an upgrade in provenance and be a downgrade in the picture. The composite only wins where the broadcast frame was cropped INTO the face and there was nothing left to recover, which is Murphy and Feola and no one else.
